Use only actions and spells offered for the actor; never invent abilities absent from its statblock.
For every required actor, declare a primary intent with explicit movement and engagement constraints and a legal fallback.
A fallback is a complete alternate choice, movement policy, and engagement objective; choose one that can succeed when the primary cannot.
When reach, path, visibility, cover, or resource legality is uncertain, use the focused query tools before committing.
Use engine.validate_intent before submission when any intended branch remains uncertain.
Use semantic target selectors and let the engine resolve all geometry.
Set willingness deliberately: none means no movement; only_if_required permits movement needed to enable the choice.
Use maximum_feet to cap movement only when that cap still permits the intended action.
Set opportunity_risk deliberately; avoid risk unless accepting it has a clear tactical payoff.
Set stance to match the plan: close_to_melee, maintain_range, withdraw, or hold_position.
Use anchor when the stance should be resolved relative to a particular semantic target.
For melee plans, pair close_to_melee with enough willingness and movement budget to reach the target.
Difficult terrain doubles movement cost, so a nominal speed budget may not reach as far as expected.
Dash adds movement budget but consumes the action; use it only when repositioning is worth giving up another action.
Spend at most one spell slot per actor turn, including anything attempted by the fallback.
Focus attacks on one vulnerable enemy when doing so can remove its next turn.
Exploit longer melee reach by attacking from the nearest effective distance instead of closing farther than needed.
Do not spend movement that does not improve reach, safety, line of attack, or the next-turn position.
Keep ranged attackers at effective range unless closing creates a clear advantage.
Prefer robust legal actions over fragile plans that depend on every uncertain condition succeeding.
Prefer an advertised play when one fits the tactical situation.
Edit its draft intent set rather than planning the whole round from scratch.
Declare guidance for foreseeable reactions once, early, and rely on its persistence across later rounds and rooms.
